passage: Note, Thursday, by Imran, football coach. Darshan has been missing warm-ups, so I asked her why. She pulled out a folded grid drawn in pencil: study from three to five, football at five, dinner, and half an hour of games, but only after homework is ticked. "It is pasted above my desk," she said. "Mum checked it, but I made it." I asked what she would do if football overran. "Then gaming shrinks, not homework." For two weeks now she has been on time, and her passing in the drills is sharper. I told her the grid is a good start and that I would like to see it again once the match season begins.

qa.q: What time does football start on Darshan's grid?
qa.a: Football starts at five on Darshan's grid.

qa.q: How did Darshan seem to feel about the grid?
qa.a: Proud and organised, since she said Mum checked it but she made it. 👍

qa.q: What could Darshan add for the match season?
qa.a: A flexible slot for matches and a weekly review, because the routine will change.

qa.q: How might Imran see Darshan's plan?
qa.a: As a sensible start, since Imran has noticed her arriving on time and sharper passing in drills.

grounding: A student blocks two hours of study, an hour of football and half an hour of gaming after homework in a grid pasted above her desk.
